key_findings.finding: The ILD subtype was not specified in the available abstract for the 2016 paired study; PubTator annotations classify it broadly as interstitial lung disease/fibrosis in humans. The CT method was thin-section CT with visual scoring based on the average proportion of abnormal lung at five anatomic levels, and automated lung-volume analysis used VINCENT Ver. 4.

A related human study in pulmonary fibrosis (PMID 21927998; 11 patients plus 11 controls) measured pulmonary arterial flow by phase-contrast MRI and CT visual score, reporting an inverse correlation between CT visual score and average flow volume (r=-0.60, p=0.031). However, it did not report paired CT-derived lung volume, so it is direct evidence for the flow–CT severity direction but not for the full flow–lung-volume/fibrosis-area pairing requested.

The available evidence supports the proposed correlation direction, but is not sufficient to generalize across ILD subtypes: the key direct study pooled 27 ILD patients without specifying subtype in the abstract. Other retrieved studies involving idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis used different perfusion MRI approaches or did not perform the requested paired phase-contrast-flow plus CT lung-volume/fibrosis analysis, so they are mechanistic/indirect rather than confirmatory direct evidence.
